html:
A church built between 1238 and 1263 under Emperor Manuel I of the Empire of Trebizond, on a terrace above the Black Sea just outside the old city of Trebizond (Trabzon).

Its plan is Byzantine, a cross in a square under a dome, but it has deep porches on three sides and carved stonework with geometric patterns and honeycomb vaulting borrowed from Seljuk buildings, like those of the Sultanate of Rum. A carved frieze on the south porch shows scenes from Genesis. Inside, its 13th century wall paintings are among the best of the late Byzantine period. Georgian and Armenian touches show the mixed world of the Black Sea coast.

After Mehmed II took the city in 1461 the church was later turned into a mosque. Its frescoes were cleaned and studied in the 1950s and 1960s, and in 1964 it became a museum. In 2013 it was turned back into a mosque, seven years before the same happened to the great Hagia Sophia in Istanbul.
sum: A church built between 1238 and 1263 under Emperor Manuel I of the Empire of Trebizond, on a terrace above the Black Sea just outside the old city of Trebizond (Trabzon).
